Criminal Appeal No. 6762 of 2009.
Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 52204 of 2012.
lawyer:
Atiar Rahman, Advocate---------For the Appellant. 
AQM Sohel Rana, Advocate---------For the Petitioner. 
Md Aminul Islam, DAG with Fatema Rashid, AAG---------For the State.
full_judgment:
ANM Bashir Ullah J: Criminal Appeal No. 6762 of 2009 and Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 52204 of 2012 under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure (in short, the Code) have been arisen out of the same judgment and order of conviction and sentence dated 20-8-2009 passed by the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Tribunal, Brahmanbaia in Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Case No. 685 of 2007 convicting the appellants and the petitioner under section 9(3) of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain, 2000 (in short, the Ain) sentencing each of them to suffer rigorous imprisonment for life with a fine of Taka 100,000. Both the appeals and the aforesaid Criminal Miscellaneous case have been heard analogously and will be governed by this single judgment. 

 2. The prosecution case, in short, is that Niaz Kazi, the full brother of victim Hosna Begum, lodged the First Information Report (in short, the FIR) with Ashuganj Police Station on 6-5-2007 without naming any accused thereof alleging inter-alia that Hosna Begum, aged about 17 years was a student of Higher Secondary School Certificate (in short, the HSC) of Abbasuddin College at Shohagpur under Ashuganj Police Station of Brahman-baria district. On 5-5-2007 at 9-00 am Hosna Begum left her house with books in order to go to her College but within afternoon of the same day since Hosna Begum did not come back to her residence, the informant and others had searched her hihther to thihther including to the nearest relatives of the Hosna Begum but she was found untraced. 

 4. The informant Niaz Kazi narrating the above facts lodged the First Information Report with Ashuganj Police Station on 6-5-2007 at 23-30 hours and on the basis of the said FIR Ashuganj PS case No. 5 dated 6-5-2007 was started. After recording of the case, the case was endorsed to PW 13 Police Sub-Inspector Md Abdul Wahab for Investigation who without any late prepared the inquest report on the dead body on 7-5-2007 at 0015 hours, that is, within 45 minutes of the filing of the case and sent the dead body to the Brahmanbaria morgue through Police Constable Jamaluddin (PW 4) for post mortem examination and accordingly post mortem on the dead body was held by PW 3 Dr. Emdadul Haque. 

 6. The case was investigated by PW 13 up to 13-5-2017 thereafter the same was investigated by PW 11 Ratan Das Gupta, Officer-in-charge of the concern Police Station who investigated the case from 14-5-2007 to 26-8-2007. Thereafter the case was investigated by PW 12 Md Jahirullah, Assistant Superintendent of Police till submission of police report on 30-10-2007. 

 7. After submission of the police report, the learned Magistrate sent the case record to the Nari-o-Shishu Tribunal, Brahmanbaria where on 9-12-2007 the case was registered as Nari-o-Shishu Case No. 687 of 2007 and when the case was pending in the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Tribunal, Brahmanbaria the government transferred the case to the Druta Bichar Tribunal, Chattagram and accordingly the record was sent to the Druta Bichar Tribunal, Chattagram on 13-5-2008 and charge under section 9(3) of the Ain was framed on 9-6-2008 by the Druta Bichar Tribunal, Chattagram and within almost 7-12-2008 most of the witnesses were examined by the Druta Bichar Tribunal, Chattagram. Thereafter since the trial of case could not be completed within the stipulated period of time, the Druto Bichar Tribunal Chattagram again sent back the case to the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Tribunal, Brahmonbaria by his order dated 7-12-2008. 

 8. The Druta Bichar Tribunal at his turn examined 13 witnesses in full and thereafter returned back the case record to the Tribunal at Brahmanbaria. The Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Tribunal, Brahmanbaria on receipt of the record on 20-1-2009 of the examining more 3 witnesses particularly PWs 14, 15 and 16 heard the argument of both the parties and thereafter pronounced the impugned judgment and order dated 20-8-2009 and convicted 1. Md Sekkal alias Sudan Mia, 2. Fakir Md Moshahed-ullah 3. Md Rubel 4. Morshed Kamal 5. Md Jamaluddin alias Jamal Mia 6. Robiullah alias Rabin and 7. Habibur Rahman alais Kamal Chowdhury under section 9(3) of the Ain sentencing each of them to suffer rigorous imprisonment for life with a fine of Taka 100,000. 

 9. On the date of pronouncement of judgment convict Robiullah alias Robin and Habibur Rahman alias Kamal Chowdhury were fugitive but the rest 5 accused were present before the Tribunal. After the pronouncement of the judgment convicts Fakir Md Moshahedullah, Morshed Kamal and Md Jamaluddin alais Jamal Mia jointly filed the Criminal appeal No. 6762 of 2009 in this Court and later on accused Habibur Rahman alias Kamal Chowdhury preferred Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 52204 of 2012 under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure and in this Miscellaneous Case Rule was issued calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the conviction and sentence awarded upon the convict petitioner Habibur Rahman alias Kamal Chowdhury will not be quashed. 

 10. As we have told it earlier that both the appeal and the Miscellaneous Case have been heard analogously by us. Though the aforesaid Criminal appeal was filed jointly by convict appellants Fakir Md Moshahedullah, Morshed Kamal and Jamaluddin alias Jamal Mia but out of these 3 appellants Morshed Kamal and Jamaluddin alias Jamal Mia have not been represented by any Advocate. Fakir Md Moshahedullah has been represented by the learned Advocate Mr Atiar Rahman and convict petitioner Habibur Rahman alias Kamal Chowdhury has been represented by the learned Advocate Mr AQM Sohel Rana. However, the appellants before us who has not been represented at the time of hearing of the appeal their case will be also considered on merit alike the other appellant and petitioner. 

 11. Mr Atiar Rahman, the learned Advocate appearing for the convict appellant Fakir Md Moshahedullah submits that the trial Tribunal though found this appellant guilty for commission of the crime of rape followed by murder of Hosna Begum in an occurrence of 5-5-2007 but he is not FIR named accused, even the informant Niaz Kazi, the full brother of Hosna Begum did not suspect this appellant in any manner at the time of filing of the FIR, in fact Fakir Md Moshahedullah was not involved with the occurrence of this case, he was arrested on mere suspicion thereafter he was entangled with the occurrence of this case. 

 13. He also submits that section 167 of the Code of Criminal Procedure empowers the Police to keep an accused in their custody for 24 hours after his arrest and if for any reason the Police needs to interrogate him, they can pray to the concerned Magistrate for the remand of the accused but in this particular case the convict appellant Fakir Md Moshahedullah was in Police custody for more than 24 hours after his arrest without any order of remand. 

 16. He also submits that it is the definite case of Fakir Md Moshahedullah that he was arrested by the RAB on 9-5-2007 and he was in illegal custody of the RAB till 11-5-2007 thereafter he was handed over to Police and his arrest by the RAB has also been admitted by PW 6. PW 6 is the important witness of the case who is the uncle of victim, surely he will not give any evidence causing any damage to the prosecution case, so from the evidence of PWs 1, 6 and 8 it has been proved beyond all reasonable doubt that Fakir Md Moshaded-ullah was arrested on 9-5-2007 by the members of RAB thereafter he was detained to the Police custody illegally till 12-5-2007 thereafter he was produced before the Magistrate PW 8 for recording his confession. So his confession cannot be considered as voluntary, fair and legal and this sort of confession cannot be the basis of conviction and sentence of an accused like Fakir Md Moshahedullah. 

 17. The learned Advocate next submits that not only PWs 1, 6 and 8 testified in the Tribunal at the time of deposition that Fakir Md Moshahedullah was arrested on 9-5-2007 but from the very beginning of the case Fakir Md Moshahedullah has been canvassing the same through bail application and other documents that he has been arrested on 9-5-2007 and he was in illegal detention of the Police and thereafter he was produced before the Magistrate on 12-5-2007 for recording his confession and after recording of the so called confession he also retracted the same on 14-5-2007 where he has given a vivid description as to how he became the subject-matter of inhuman torture by the RAB and Police when he was in the illegal custody of the RAB and Police and he also in his petition of retraction categorically stated that he was arrested on 9-5-2007, so it is not a new defence case on behalf of Fakir Md Moshahedullah that he was arrested on 9-5-2007 rather from the very beginning of the case he has been ventilated the same. So by all the possible ways it has been proved that he was in illegal custody of the Police for 3 days before his confession, so his such illegal detention in the hands of the Police and RAB make his confession in voluntary and untrue, so he deserves acquittal from the case. 

 18. The learned Advocate in his concluding submissions submits that since there is no eye witness of the occurrence and since the motive of the occurrence has been introduced by PW 1 for the first time at the time of trial which could be set in motion at that time of lodging FIR. So, the motive as introduced is a subsequent embellishment in this case by the prosecution in order to entangle this accused and others with the occurrence of this case. Since the confession of Fakir Md Moshahedullah is the only basis of the confession which has been found illegal, so the judgment and order of the conviction and sentence as passed against Fakir Md Moshahedullah is liable to be set aside. 

 21. The learned Advocate also adds that in fact, the informant introduced a new story of snatching of a mobile set at the time of trial for the first time in order to entangle the accused with the occurrence of this case, so the evidence of PW 1 regarding the snatching of mobile set is not believable and credible at all. Had the occurrence of rape and murder of Hosna Begum been taken place for the said occurrence of snatching of mobile set, the informant must not forget it to state in his FIR, so the sweeping statement of the PW 1 regarding the snatching of mobile set at trial is not at all believable. 

 23. The learned Advocate also submits that it is fact that the confessing accused Md Morshed Kamal, Fakir Md Moshahedullah and Md Rubel in their confessional statements told the name of this Habibur Rahman alias Kamal Chowdhury as one of the rapist but other than those confessions of 3 co-accused there is no any independent evidence against this appellant marking his involvement with the occurrence of this case, so the confession of the co-accused cannot be the basis to find the petitioner guilty for commission of the crime under section 9(3) of the Ain. 

 24. He also submits that the confession of the co-accused is a corroborative evidence for other which needs to be considered along with independent evidence if any but there appears no independent evidence regarding the involvement of this petitioner with the commission of crime. So the trial Tribunal wrongly relied upon the confession of 3 co-accused in finding the present petitioner guilty. In support of such submission he referred the case of Majid Sheikh alias Majid vs State reported in 11 BLC (AD) 149. 

 25. On the other hand, Mrs. Anwara Shahjahan, the learned Deputy Attorney-General appearing for the respondent and the opposite party supporting the judgment of the trial Tribunal and assailing the submissions and arguments advanced by the learned Advocate for the appellant and the petitioner submits that it is a case where maximum atrocity has been shown in committing the rape on the victim Hosna Begum followed by murder. 7 (seven) accused continuously committed gang rape on the victim thereafter they did not stop there rather murdered the deceased strangulating her through semis (a short inner) and bra(brassiere) and when the dead body was recovered the same ligatures were found around the neck of the victim. 

 26. The learned Deputy Attorney-General also submits that the occurrence of this case took place on 5-5-2007 when the victim was going to her college but before 6 months of the occurrence of this case a mobile set was snatched from the informant by accused Rubel, Sekkal, Kamal and Robiullah and in a local Salish they were found guilty for the snatching of the said mobile set and by the local salishder they were sentenced to fine Taka 5,000 each but Rubel, Sekkal, Kamal and did not take the matter easy rather they took it as an exceptional case and also showed their determination for taking revenge against the informant and his family members and as part of the said device they on the way of Hosna Begum towards her college committed gang rape on her and murdered her. 

 27. The learned Deputy Attorney-General also submits that now-a-day no criminal commit crime keeping its evidence and the same has also happened in this particular case. The accused has chosen a lonely place which was free from other people and they had so that the occurrence of inhuman crime cannot be seen or witnessed by others and thereafter they committed gang rape one after another. 

 33. She categorically submits that PW 1 in his evidence categorically stated that all the accused were involved in the occurrence of this case as they had a strong intention to take revenge of the occurrence of snatching mobile set from PW 1, so if the evidence of PW 1 is considered along with the confessions of 3 accused it will be revealed that all the 7 convicts were involved with the occurrence of this case, so the trial Tribunal on the right assessment of the evidence on record found the appellants and petitioner guilty under section 9(3) of the Ain. 

 37. The learned Deputy Attorney-General also submits that the petitioner Habibur Rahman alias Kamal Chowdhury alias Shamim without filing an appeal against the judgment and order of conviction and sentence preferred Miscellaneous case 52204 of 2012 under section 561A of the Code but in a proceeding under section 561A against the judgment and order of conviction and sentence the scope of the Court is very much limited. In a proceeding under section 561A of the Code Court cannot sift the evidence like the appeal, so the petitioner Habibur Rahman alias Kamal Chowdhury alias Shamirn is not entitled to get any relief in the Rule also. So, the appeal is liable to be dismis-sed and the Rule is liable to be discharged with costs. 

 41. However, from the post mortem examination report it appears that the victim was done to death through strangulation which was ante-mortem and homicidal in nature. Whatever may be in the cross-examination of PW 3 regarding the case of death of the deceased, the defence at trial and also at the time of hearing of this appeal and the Rule admitted it frankly that the victim was done to death but the appellants and the Rule petitioner were not involved with the occurrence of murder of the deceased. 

 42. In this appeal and Rule it is important to note here that the victim was not only done to death rather she became the subject-matter of gang rape. PW 5 Md Awal, a chemical examiner deposing in the trial Court stated that he received a packet of clothes for chemical examination in connection of this case comprising a borka (veil), a kamij, a salower, a brassiere and a scarp and at the time of chemical examination he found the existence of human semen in the salower and did not find human semen in the other clothes and he furnished a report to that effect on 17-5-2007. He proved the report and his signature on it marked, exhibit 9 and 9(ka). 

 46. It is admitted in this case that there is no eye witness of the occurrence. Police arrested Morshed Kamal immediate after occurrence who gave some information to the Police regarding the commission of offence, thereafter Police arrested one after another accused and out of the arrested accused Morshed Kamal, Fakir Md Moshahedullah and Md Rubel made confessional statements in this case. 

 52. From the materials on record we find that the prosecution case has been unfurled through the confessions of 3 accused in this case and Fakir Md Moshahedullah is one of the confessing accused while Morshed Kamal and Rubel are the rest two confessing accused. If we consider the confessions of these 3 accused side by side along with the inquest report, post mortem report and other materials on record we find that all of them have given a very consistent statement regarding the commission of the crime of murder and rape of the victim. 

 53. Under the above facts and circumstances, we are not in a position to accept the oral evidence of some of the witnesses regarding the arrest of accused Fakir Md Moshahedullah on 9-5-2007 which is not supported by the documentary evidence on record. Fakir Md Moshahedullah retracted his confession within two days from the date of recording of his confession. The motive of this case has been revealed in the trial of the case. PW 1 Niaz Kazi in his evidence testified that before six months of the date of occurrence a mobile set has been snatched by accused Rubel, Sekkal, Kamal and Robiullah and on that issue in a local Salish fine was imposed upon them and in continuation of the said occurrence of snatching of mobile set Hosna Begum rebuked the accused Rubel, Sekkal, Kamal and Robi-ullah as a 'chor' (thieves) which make them angry and furious and from then they were searching chance for taking revenge upon Hosna Begum and as part of said plan they forming a group coming into the spot on the date of occurrence raided Hosna Begum and mounting over her committed gang rape on her. 

 56. From the above noted portion of the inquest report it is clear to us that every words of the confession of Fakir Md Moshahedullah and Morshed Kamal are consistent with the other materials on record and with the occurrence of this case, so how we can discard and disbelieve such confessions in this or that plea. 

 59. PW 8 recorded the confessional statement of accused Fakir Md Moshahedullah and Md Morshed Kamal who in his evidence testified that he after observing all legal formalities and requirements recorded the confessions of those accused and he was cross-examined elaborately by the defence on the above facts. We find nothing in his cross-examination for which his recording of confession can be discredited, so we are of the sharp view that the confession of Fakir Md Moshahedullah and Morshed Kamal were voluntary and at the same time it was true as the every words of confessions are found consistent with the occurrence of this case. 

 60. In the case of lslamuddin vs State 13 BLC, (AD) 81 it has been held by the Appellate Division that it is the settled principle of law that judicial confession if it is found to be true and voluntary can indeed form of the sole basis of conviction as against the maker of confession and the same view has been taken in many cases including case of Abdur Rashid vs State, 3 BLD 206 and Shahjahan Ali vs State, 59 DLR 396. In this particular case Fakir Md Moshahedullah and Md Morshed Kamal retracted their confession but if once confession is found voluntary and true the subsequent retraction is immaterial. 

 61. In the case of Bhagoban Chandra Chakma vs State, 38 DLR 374 it has been held that the confessional statement may be the sole basis of conviction of its maker if such statement is found to be voluntary and true even though the confessional statement may be retracted at a subsequent stage. The confessional statement by Fakir Md Moshahedullah was made on 12-5-2007 and within two days he retracted the confession. It appears to be very much unusual to us that he retracted the confession within two days of making it and ultimately it shows that he is a harden criminal. 

 62. However, for the reasons discussed above we find that the confession of Fakir Md Moshahedullah and Morshed Kamal are voluntary, true and fully consistent with the occurrence of this case. So the trial Tribunal rightly found them guilty relying on their confessions. We find it difficult to interfere in the judgment and the order of conviction and sentence as awarded by the Tribunal upon confessing accused Fakir Md Moshahedullah and another appellant Md Morshed Kamal. 

 63. So far the another appellant Jamaluddin alias Jamal Mia is concerned it is fact that all the 3 confessing accused in their confessions told the name of accused Jamaluddin. The 3 confessing accused told in their confession that Jamaluddin was a member of the accused and gang group who committed brutal rape on victim but other than the confession of co-accused there appears no independent evidence against accused Jamaluddin even there is no allegation that Jamaluddin was in the group of snatching of the mobile set of the informant six months ahead of the occurrence of this case. 

 64. In the case of Ostar Ali vs State 3 BLC (AD) 53 it has been held very categorically that the confession of an accused is not substantive evidence against the co-accused who did not confess and such evidence alone without substantive corroborative evidence cannot form basis of conviction of co-accused. The same view has been taken in many cases by the Appellate Division and this Division. Under the foregoing narrative we find it difficult to discover any independent and substantive evidence against Jamaluddiri other than the confession of co-accused, so we find it difficult to maintain the conviction and sentence of appellant Jamaluddin in this case. 

 65. Convict petitioner Habibur Rahman alias Kamal Chowdhury alias Shamim challenged the judgment of the trial Tribunal under section 561A of the Code taking the ground that there is no legal evidence against him in this case. 

 66. The learned Advocate for the petitioner at his turn submits that PW 1 in his evidence testified that Rubel, Sekkal, Kamal and Robiullah snatched the mobile set and in a local arrangement they were fined and following the said occurrence victim Hosna Begum also rebuked the accused and they in order to take revenge murdered Hosna Begum. The learned Advocate thus submits that though PW 1 told the name of Kamal Chowdhury regarding the snatching of mobile set but that did not establish and prove that this accused was involved in the commission of crime of rape and murder as there is no evidence against Kamal Chowdhury regarding his involvement with the occurrence of this case save and except the evidence of PWs 1 and PW 6. 

 69. We are not at all interested to deviate ourselves from the principle that the confession of the co-accused should not be the basis of conviction of another accused. But if from the it is found that there is independent evidence to show the entanglement of a particular accused with the occurrence of a case and if such evidence is corroborated by the confession of others then the conviction of such an accused should be upheld. 

 70. The evidence of PW 6 regarding Kamal Chowdhury that he found Kamal Chowdhury in the company of other accused at the eve of occurrence is very much relevant and consistent with the facts of the case and significant also. Over and again, this evidence has not been strongly challenged and denied by the defence particularly by Kamal Chowdhury. Kamal Chowdhury was all through an absconding accused in this case. He could not avail the opportunity to challenge the evidence of PW 6 remaining absconding for a long day. Though it is the settled principle of law also that absconsion of an accused is not the prove of guilt but at the same time there is a lot of decisions that whenever an accused having knowledge of any commission of crime remains fugitive is very much relevant against him. 

 71. If we consider the evidence of PW 6 along with fugitiveness of accused Kamal Chowdhury and other corroborating statements of the confessing accused we find that the conviction and sentence of Habibur Rahman alias Kamal Chowdhury alias Shamim is justified in a case like this. 

 74. The Rule in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 52204 of 2012 is also discharged. The 'judgment and order of conviction and sentence dated 20-8-2009 passed by Nari-o-Shisu Nirjaton Damon Tribunal, Brahman baria in Nari-o-Shisu Case No. 685 of 2007 so far it is related for the convict petitioner Habibur Rahman alias Kamal Chowdhury alias Shamim are upheld.
